description:
Mapping music/audio to stage lighting control (DMX, hue/value/intensity, strobe, beam). Covers rule-based sound-to-light (FFT/beatgrid triggers) and learned/generative approaches (Skip-BART, SeqLight).

*Axis:* `topic`

Design and validation of metrics: Light-BAS (beat alignment of light kinematics), FID over light features, diversity, collapse rate, human pairwise preference, and the nulls (metronome, circular shift, split-half) each one must be priced against.

*Axis:* `topic`

Treating the target as a distribution to SAMPLE from (diffusion, flow matching, diffusion forcing, VQ+AR) rather than a function to regress. Use when p(y|x) is multi-modal and per-frame MSE collapses to the conditional mean.

*Axis:* `topic`

Music-conditioned dance/motion generation (EDGE, FlowerDance, InfiniteDance, DiscoForcing) and its datasets (AIST++, FineDance, InfiniteDance). In LightSem the generated dancer is a LATENT intermediate: present at train time, sampled at test time.

*Axis:* `topic`

Human pose / skeletal keypoint time series as a modality (2D/3D keypoints, kinetic energy, jerk, motion events). Includes dance motion and pose used as an intermediate representation.

*Axis:* `topic`

Empirical music-psychology literature on how audio features drive spontaneous body movement across many people (Burger/Toiviainen/Luck Jyvaskyla mocap, Solberg & Jensenius club EDM, groove research). Source of the shared-vs-personal split that defines LightSem's target blocks.

*Axis:* `topic`

The chosen supervision target is not a function of the available input: multiple equally valid targets exist for the same input (one-to-many mapping), so any single recorded target is an arbitrary draw. Training against it caps achievable performance at the inter-annotator/inter-performer agreement ceiling, and a model appearing to 'fail' may simply be hitting that ceiling. Diagnosed by measuring agreement between independent targets for identical input before modelling.

*Axis:* `problem`

Strictly causal, bounded-latency streaming inference (audio-in to DMX-out). Covers online beat tracking, causal audio encoders, diffusion forcing, teacher->causal-student distillation, lookahead/delay-line trade-offs.

*Axis:* `topic`

Mapping body kinematics (speed, jerk, spread, verticality, laterality, Laban effort) to fixture parameters (dimmer, pan/tilt, zoom, strobe, colour). The conductor layer.

*Axis:* `topic`

A trivial or degenerate policy attains the metric's optimum (a metronome maximises beat alignment; persistence maximises level R2; jitter aligns to beats). The metric then cannot separate a working system from a trivial one. Guard: report the trivial policy's score alongside, use the metric as a constraint, carry the claim on a distributional or human metric.

*Axis:* `problem`

Using a regression/MSE objective where p(target|input) is multi-modal: the optimal predictor is the conditional mean, a blurred low-energy average no real sample looks like, so held-out R2 is ~0 even when every draw from the true conditional would be acceptable. Diagnosed by an inter-annotator/inter-performer ceiling near zero at the target resolution. Remedy is a generative objective and distributional evaluation, not a different regression target.

*Axis:* `problem`

Where a result sits on the lookahead axis: strictly causal, bounded lookahead bought with a delay line, or whole-track offline. A score is only comparable to another score at the same point on this axis.

*Axis:* `topic`

replacing hand-written descriptor-to-fixture rules with a learned decoder

*Axis:* `topic`

A number was produced with information the deployed system cannot have at that instant. Covers library defaults that read ahead (centred STFT frames, centred median filters, global top_db clamps), interpolating onto a control grid from a later analysis frame, and any offline fit quoted as if it were online. Distinct from matched-baseline: the baseline may be fine and the FEATURE still illegal.

*Axis:* `problem`

stems, per-stem features and their use as conditioning

*Axis:* `topic`
